name: Niulai
_comment: Trims are read off docs/clips/contact-sheet.png. The Meshy exports are whole performances — the punch is four seconds of standing in a guard stance with the punch in the middle of it — so each state names the slice worth playing. Speeds are not set here: the game's timings below decide how fast a slice plays, so the animation and the rules cannot disagree about when contact happens.
_spares: hurdle, backjump and jump are merged and trimmed but not bound to anything: jumping needs an air state first. knee is an obvious heavy attack whenever a third button is wanted.

power.name: MAMA
power._comment: Niulai's super. The meter fills from hitting and from being hit, and spends itself on one shout: ten mamas across the whole stage. Cast is how long he is locked in the summon pose; release is how far into it the herd arrives — timed to the frame his arms go up, because a summon whose effect precedes the gesture reads as a bug. gallopAt is the speed the run cycle was authored to look right at, so slowing the herd slows its legs to match instead of skating; range is how far a cow travels before it retires, which is what stops one outliving the picture now that a walking player can move the camera faster than the herd advances.

name: Baola
blurb: Quick. Faster on her feet, easier to hurt.
_comment: A leopard: quicker than Niulai and lighter. Same eleven clips, same trims — they came from the same generator with the same names, so the slices that worked for him work for her.

power.name: SUPER
power._comment: Baola's super is not a screen-clear like Niulai's — it is seven seconds of being a different animal. Double damage out, half damage in, and a model swap so the player can see which of those seven seconds they are in without reading a bar. She is not locked in place for it: the whole point is that she gets to spend the time fighting. grow and shrink are the seconds the new body spends easing up to its own size and back down to hers, and both happen inside the seven, so the number on the bar is the number of seconds she is actually stronger for.

name: Wolfwolf
_comment: Same treatment as Niulai: whole performances trimmed to the part worth playing, with the game's timings deciding playback speed. The wolf has no block clip and does not block — that stays the player's move.

name: The Cart
_comment: A static mesh, not a rig: no bones, no clips, brought in by tools/import-prop.mjs. Its motion is written in actor.js, because a vehicle's whole vocabulary is pitch, roll and shake. scale 2.8 makes it 1.20 units tall, 2.80 long and 1.42 deep — taller than a fighter and nearly three times as long, which is what makes it read as the end of the level rather than a big wolf.
_faceOffset: The model's nose points along its own -X. The characters are authored facing +Z, so the game's quarter turn lines them up down the belt and turns the cart across it; this cancels that.
_body: radius and hurtRadius are its half-length, hurtDepth its half-depth. Set them smaller than the bodywork and the player is shoved to a stop while still standing inside it. hurtRadius is what makes it hittable at all: a punch measured centre to centre could never reach, because its side is in the player's face while its centre sits further away than an arm is long.

name: Mama
_comment: One clip and one job: run left to right through everything. She is not a Fighter — she has no health, cannot be hit and does not collide with anyone. The fallbacks below point every state the actor knows about at the only clip she has, so nothing has to special-case an actor with a vocabulary of one.

name: Super Baola
_comment: What Baola turns into. Same rig, same clip names, same rest height as she has, so her trims are reused unchanged — a jaguar warrior built by the same generator from the same skeleton. scale is her 0.588 times a third again, which is what 'enlarge' has to mean on screen: big enough to read at a glance from across the belt, not so big she stops fitting between two wolves. Five clips rather than eight: no block, no knee, no jump.
